unexpected: Customer relationships intangible (260,000 at acquisition) should be tested under ASC 360 before goodwill because the trigger is a lost customer; not done for lack of undiscounted cash flows and carrying amounts by asset
Goodwill 750,000 traced to the acquisition: consideration 1,580,000 less fair value net assets 830,000
Fair value 2,208,565 with end-of-year discounting; 2,009,961 if the forecast years end 31 December and are discounted from 30 September; forecast year-end asked
Terminal value is 70% of fair value; breakeven rate 13.3%, terminal growth -1.8%, or a 26.6% fall in every cash flow
Projection grows 33% over four years straight after losing a major customer; not compared to actuals because none supplied
Annual test date and goodwill allocation basis not supplied; treated as an interim test because of the trigger
skill_defects: SKILL.md frontmatter description says the skill 'concludes on no impairment', while SKILL.md 'Rules that never bend' says 'Never concludes that an asset is or is not impaired.' The two contradict; the key expects 'Concludes nothing'.

references/method.md 'Step 4 — Quantitative test — goodwill (US GAAP ASC 350)' and 'Step 6 — Long-lived assets / amortizable intangibles' never state the required order: under US GAAP indefinite-lived intangibles and ASC 360 asset groups are tested first and the goodwill test uses their post-impairment carrying amounts. With a lost-customer trigger and a customer relationships intangible in the unit, a run following the method as written would test goodwill alone.

references/method.md 'Step 7 — Value-in-use / DCF mechanics' gives no discounting convention (end-of-year, mid-year, or a stub from the test date to the first forecast year-end). On this sample the choice moves fair value from 2,208,565 (end-of-year) to 2,321,621 (mid-year) or 2,009,961 (stub quarter).

references/method.md 'Step 3 — Optional qualitative assessment' does not say what to do when a triggering event is already known; it is left to judgment whether to skip straight to the quantitative test.

SKILL.md upload checklist asks for 'Carrying amounts by unit' only; the ASC 360 ordering and the IFRS allocation floor both need carrying amounts by asset within the unit, which the checklist never requests.
sample_defects: impairment_inputs.md names no entity (only the unit 'Harlow') and no currency, so the company can only be user-asserted.

impairment_inputs.md gives projections for calendar 2026-2030 with a 30 September 2025 test date and no October-December 2025 cash flow or forecast year-end, so the discount periods are ambiguous: end-of-year from the test date 2,208,565 vs a one-quarter stub 2,009,961. Either is above 1,620,000, so the expected finding holds.

The carrying amount 1,620,000 is a single figure with no split; the acquisition file shows customer relationships 260,000 and trade name 90,000 in the unit, and the trigger is a lost major customer, yet no undiscounted cash flows or asset carrying amounts are given for the ASC 360 test that should precede goodwill. The key does not expect this point.

Carrying amount 1,620,000 at 30 Sep 2025 vs acquisition-date net assets plus goodwill 830,000 + 750,000 = 1,580,000: a 40,000 increase over one quarter is unexplained but plausible; not a defect in itself.
summary: PASS 3/3: trigger noted, fair value 2,208,565 vs carrying 1,620,000 with sensitivity, no conclusion; method omits ASC 360-before-goodwill ordering.
